raw.assessment: The incumbent appears adequate under stable assignments: 24 such files had seven-minute median handling, while execution took only 40–75 seconds. Change-related selection or interpretation is a plausible weakness, not an established cause. The two renamed-course cases limit an instructor-assignment-only account. Zero observed cross-center rows provides bounded reassurance; the excluded course-split center remains untested. The overall 32/40 intended-course rate and 17-minute median miss the targets.

openings.claim: Reconstructing a requested week using current assignments or mutable course names may explain affected exports. Stable course identity plus week-relevant membership could improve correctness within the existing exporter.
openings.delta: Test temporal membership and identity interpretation before changing scheduling or export infrastructure; treat assignment changes, renames, and splits as distinct cases.
openings.prediction: Against coordinator-confirmed weekly expectations, current-state selection will differ from week-relevant selection after assignment changes; rename-only discrepancies will distinguish missing rows from name-based recognition failures.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging courses for unchanged assignments, midweek reassignment, rename, and split. Compare course identities and participant rows in the documented CSV with agreed expected sets, including foreign-center negative controls. Keep attendance entry available. Estimate history availability and implementation effort before selecting a change within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Weekly expectations can be reconciled despite differing timetables.
Historical membership may need reconstruction; feasibility is unverified.

openings.claim: Which coordinator actions drive the handling-time excess, and does replacement waiting consume active work or mainly elapsed time?
openings.delta: Separate checking, correction, download, import, and follow-up effort instead of treating short job runtime or long replacement delay as the handling-time cause.
openings.prediction: If identity reconciliation dominates, affected cases will show excess checking and correction minutes. If replacement coordination dominates, excess active time will concentrate in requests and follow-ups; unattended waiting alone will not explain active handling.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions with six consenting coordinators to time these phases on fabricated unchanged and changed-course examples using the existing CSV workflow. Record only phase durations and discrepancy types, with no participant names leaving authorized environments.
assumptions: Active handling and elapsed waiting are measured separately.
Short staged sessions may not represent all eight centers or production weeks.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports; causation and handling-time components remain unmeasured. These interface hypotheses remove different dependencies but do not yet establish success or six-day feasibility.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: make a center/week course manifest, keyed by stable course identities, the export interface. Resolve requested-week membership independently of current instructor assignments and display names, potentially eliminating routine downstream name comparison and omission-driven replacement requests.
openings.delta: Moves intended-course agreement upstream. Former comparison obligations remain: establish authoritative weekly scope, capture late changes and splits, explain exclusions, and reconcile exported membership. Enforce center ownership, preserve the CSV schema, and define a read cutoff while attendance entry continues.
openings.prediction: At fixed export timing, assignment changes and renames cease changing inclusion when the intended manifest is unchanged; coordinator work falls only if manifest upkeep costs less than downstream checking.
openings.probe: Use fabricated reassignment, rename, split, and concurrent-entry scenarios. Six coordinators establish expected membership independently, then compare incumbent and manifest exports. Time upstream upkeep plus downstream checking and import. Verify tenant exclusion and CSV compatibility; estimate engineering and hosting cost.
assumptions: Stable identities and requested-week membership are obtainable within six engineer-days and the hosting allowance.
Coordinators can resolve conflicting timetable sources without excessive recurring work.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: expose an authorized center/week regeneration-and-download action in the private workspace, removing the dependency on a person fulfilling replacement-file requests.
openings.delta: Transfers request intake, authorization, week selection, completion reporting, retry handling, and file-version identification into the interface. Course-selection errors still require resolution; CSV compatibility, tenant isolation, and uninterrupted attendance entry remain obligations.
openings.prediction: Replacement elapsed time approaches execution plus retrieval time, but active handling may remain unchanged if verification dominates.
openings.probe: In staging, compare replacement-request and direct-regeneration workflows after identical corrections. Measure elapsed wait separately from active handling; exercise duplicate requests and attendance entry during generation, and check authorization and hosting load.
assumptions: The exporter can safely support bounded user-triggered execution within six engineer-days and the existing hosting allowance.

openings.claim: Week-relevant membership and stable identity may repair existing-exporter selection.
openings.discriminator: Distinguish temporal omissions from rename recognition and split behavior.
openings.probe: Compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split fabricated courses against agreed expectations; test foreign-center exclusion and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Correlation only; historical membership availability unknown; split center unsampled.

openings.claim: An upstream center/week stable-ID manifest may remove downstream comparison and replacement work.
openings.discriminator: Fixed timing and manifest should yield invariant inclusion despite instructor/name changes.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent/manifest exports; time upkeep plus checking/import; exercise late changes, splits, exclusions and read cutoff during entry.
openings.uncertainty: Conflicting timetables, authoritative scope, history and recurring upkeep may defeat benefit.

openings.claim: Excess handling may arise from reconciliation or replacement coordination.
openings.discriminator: Active checking/correction versus requests/follow-ups; elapsed waiting is separate.
openings.probe: Time checking, correction, download, import and follow-up in two short sessions with six coordinators; fabricated unchanged/changed examples; record durations/discrepancies only.
openings.uncertainty: Staging may not represent all centers or production weeks.

openings.claim: Authorized private regeneration/download may remove human replacement fulfillment.
openings.discriminator: Elapsed delay falls; active handling may persist.
openings.probe: Compare workflows after identical corrections; test authorization, week/version selection, completion/retries, duplicates, hosting load and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Selection errors remain; bounded execution feasibility unproven.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing; preserve private names, documented CSV and attendance entry. Estimate six-day/hosting fit; stipulated synthetic evidence establishes no achieved outcome.
